summary: Henrik Zilliacus worked in linguistics and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Helsinki from circa 1926 to 1936, where he later held a post from circa 1944 to 1974 and taught Klaus Karttunen.

Henry Beveridge was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Glasgow (~1853–1857) and Queen's University Belfast (1856). He served in the Indian Civil Service (1857–1893) and was President of The Asiatic Society (1890–1891).

Henry Clarke Warren worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, working under Charles Rockwell Lanman in 1879, Maurice Bloomfield circa 1881–1884, and T. W. Rhys Davids.

Henry Creswicke Rawlinson specialized in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University, he served in the East India Company (~1827–1858) and as Director (1862) and President (1878–1881) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Henry George Keene worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and Indology. He studied at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, served in the East India Company, and became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics educated at Yale and Andover. He held a professorship of Hebrew at Yale Divinity School in 1861 and served at Union Theological Seminary as instructor (1858) and professor of Hebrew (1862).

Henry Herbert Dodwell, active in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Educational Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions at SOAS (1922–1946).

Henry Hoenigswald worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence between 1932 and 1937, and held a post at the University of Pennsylvania from circa 1948 to 1985.

Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He studied at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College from circa 1797 to 1802, and under John Borthwick Gilchrist from circa 1804 to 1805.
Henry Miers Elliot was an Indologist and historian who studied at Winchester College (~1820–1826). He served as a civil servant with the East India Company from circa 1826 to 1853.

Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1783 to 1815 and held the post of Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, from 1803 to 1804.

Henry Shiu specializes in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Toronto in 2006, having studied under Shek-Wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David B. Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.

Henry Sullivan Jarrett, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, succeeded Heinrich Blochmann. From circa 1870 to 1894, he served as Secretary and Member of the Board of Examiners in Calcutta.

Henry Thomas Colebrooke was an Indologist who studied under Citrapati. He served the East India Company and Bengal Civil Service, taught Sanskrit at Fort William College (1782–1814), and was President of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1837).

Herbert Cushing Tolman was an Indologist, linguist, and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at Yale, Peabody, Hobart, Nashville, and Louisville. He held posts at Yale, Wisconsin-Madison, North Carolina at Chapel Hill, and Vanderbilt University (1894–1923).
Herbert Hope Risley was an Indologist and historian who completed his studies at Winchester College from circa 1863 to 1869 and at New College from circa 1869 to 1873.

Herbert Härtel was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt at Göttingen. He served as Director of the Museum für Asiatische Kunst Berlin (1963–1986) and held an honorary professorship at the Free University of Berlin.

Herbert Niel Randle worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as professor of philosophy at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1910–1927) and as Librarian of the India Office Library from 1927 to 1949.

Herbert V. Guenther worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, studying at Munich and Vienna under Wilhelm Geiger and Wilhelm Havers. He held posts at Vienna, Lucknow, Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and the University of Saskatchewan (1964–1984).

Herbert Weir Smyth was a linguist who studied at Swarthmore, Harvard, Leipzig, and Göttingen under Hermann Sauppe. He held teaching posts at Williams College, Bryn Mawr, and became Eliot Professor of Greek Literature at Harvard in 1901.
